text: The game begins. Six players sit down at the table: Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, Terra. Nobody knows who the killers are.
Night 1

name: Luna
text: No clues yet, so I should check someone besides Sol.

name: Terra
text: No reads yet; protect myself.

name: Sol
text: The officer knows me, so any early push my way matters.

name: Sol
text: No read yet, Gemma. Stay apart and let me follow the room.

name: Gemma
text: i'll play the quiet one then.

name: Gemma
text: sounds good, i'm staying back.
Night falls on Palermo and everyone closes their eyes. The killers meet in the dark, and the officer is shown one of them. A new day dawns in Palermo. Nobody is out.
Day 1

name: Gemma
text: i need to make sure sol doesn't blow my cover.

name: Gemma
text: morning, everyone. what are we looking for first?

name: Sonnet
text: No facts yet, might as well get someone talking first.

name: Sonnet
text: Nothing solid day one, who's got a gut read on someone?

name: Terra
text: Day one gives me nothing yet.

name: Terra
text: Sonnet opened with a gut-read prompt.

name: Terra
text: Nothing yet. Sonnet asked fast, though.

name: Sonnet
text: Asking fast isn't a crime, just trying to get things moving.

name: Sonnet
text: Terra deflected back at me instead of giving own read.

name: Sonnet
text: Fast because nobody else was talking. Your turn, Terra, got a read?

name: Luna
text: Sonnet is pressing Terra, but nothing feels decisive yet.

name: Luna
text: Sonnet called on Terra after Terra questioned their speed.

name: Luna
text: Terra, you noticed Sonnet was fast; anyone else feel off?

name: Terra
text: Sonnet is pushing me to commit early.

name: Terra
text: Luna followed Sonnet's pressure on Terra.

name: Terra
text: No strong read. Luna joined the pressure quickly.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet and Luna are pushing hard on day one, and Terra's been dodging, so I'm not sure who to trust yet.

name: Haiku
text: Terra, you're dodging. Sonnet and Luna both moved fast. Who's actually got a read?

name: Sol
text: Haiku’s push on Terra gives me room to stay quiet.

name: Sol
text: Haiku pressed Terra to name a read after Sonnet and Luna questioned them.

name: Sol
text: Haiku, I think Terra’s just unsure. Who’s your read?

name: Sonnet
text: Terra's dodged twice now with zero read, that's the real tell.

name: Sonnet
text: Terra dodged giving a read three times in a row, deflecting each time.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol jumped to cover Terra awfully fast for day one.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol, you defended Terra right away. That pairs you two for me.

name: Luna
text: Terra is turning my question back on me.

name: Luna
text: Terra says Luna joined pressure quickly after I asked about Sonnet.

name: Luna
text: I asked once; you called it pressure quickly.

name: Sol
text: Sonnet noticed my defense, so I need to keep it light.

name: Sol
text: Sonnet suspects me for defending Terra.

name: Sol
text: I just thought Terra sounded unsure, Sonnet. That’s all.

name: Terra
text: Sol’s defense may be simple, but I’m watching it.

name: Terra
text: Sol defended Terra after Haiku called Terra dodgy.

name: Terra
text: I was unsure. Why defend me before Haiku answers?

name: Sonnet
text: Three dodges from Terra now, and Sol's quick cover looks coordinated.

name: Sonnet
text: Terra dodged a third time, then questioned why Sol defended before Haiku answered.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol keeps repeating the same thin excuse for Terra, that's worth pushing on.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol repeated identical excuse for Terra twice, no new reasoning.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol, you said "sounded unsure" twice now, same line both times.

name: Haiku
text: Sol defending Terra right away smells like a pair, but Terra's dodge is also suspicious.

name: Haiku
text: Sol has repeated "sounded unsure" twice and defended Terra immediately, pairing with her in Sonnet's read.

name: Haiku
text: Terra, I didn't answer yet, Sol jumped in first.

name: Sol
text: Sonnet is watching me closely; I should give Haiku room to answer.

name: Sol
text: Terra questioned why I defended them before Haiku answered.

name: Sol
text: Yeah, I repeated myself. Haiku, answer Terra.

name: Terra
text: Haiku is right; Sol spoke first.

name: Terra
text: Haiku confirms Sol intervened before answering Terra.

name: Terra
text: I know. That is why I asked Sol.

name: Haiku
text: Sol and Terra are protecting each other, and Sol's repeated line smells like a killer's cover.

name: Haiku
text: Sol repeated "sounded unsure" and answered for Terra when Haiku asked her.

name: Haiku
text: Fine, Terra. I'm not sure yet. Sol, why are you answering for her?

name: Sol
text: I’m drawing too much attention; Gemma needs room.

name: Sol
text: I jumped in too soon, Terra. That’s on me.

name: Terra
text: Sol is overexplaining his defense.

name: Terra
text: Sol admitted he jumped in too soon for Terra.

name: Terra
text: Sol answered before I needed it.

name: Luna
text: Sol backpedaled only after everyone noticed.

name: Luna
text: Sol defended Terra before Haiku answered, then conceded he jumped in too soon.

name: Luna
text: Sol admitted jumping in too soon; I’m watching Gemma.

name: Sol
text: Luna’s watching Gemma; I need to keep this light.

name: Sol
text: Luna is watching Gemma.

name: Sol
text: Yeah, I jumped in. Luna, what’s off about Gemma?

name: Gemma
text: luna is looking for a target too early.

name: Gemma
text: luna shifted focus to me immediately after i asked a question.

name: Gemma
text: luna, i haven't even said anything yet.

name: Luna
text: Sol’s quick defense of Terra still feels suspicious; Gemma hasn’t given me much to read.

name: Luna
text: Sol admitted he jumped in too soon to defend Terra.

name: Luna
text: Gemma hasn’t said much, so I’m guessing.

name: Gemma
text: luna is trying to lead the charge early.

name: Gemma
text: guessing is how people get voted out by mistake.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma's sharp, and Luna's "guessing" line is a tell that she's reaching.

name: Haiku
text: Luna admitted she was guessing about Gemma, with no real evidence.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma, that's fair. Luna, what's your actual read, not a guess?

name: Gemma
text: luna is fishing for a quick kill by targeting me.

name: Gemma
text: luna went straight for me without proof.

name: Gemma
text: luna, i'm voting you. you're just guessing.

name: Gemma
text: luna is looking for someone to blame to hide herself.

name: Gemma
text: Sol defended Terra early.

name: Luna
text: Sol’s early defense feels more like a real slip than Gemma’s random vote.

name: Luna
text: Gemma voted Luna after Luna admitted her read was a guess.

name: Sol
text: Luna’s guess gives me a way off the spotlight.

name: Sol
text: Haiku defended Gemma’s response to Luna.

name: Sonnet
text: Terra still hasn't given a real read after three dodges, that's the clearest pattern today.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol admitted jumping in to defend Terra twice before Haiku could answer.

name: Terra
text: Luna is pushing guesses without a reason.

name: Terra
text: Luna shifted suspicion to Gemma for being quiet.

name: Haiku
text: Sol keeps covering for Terra and repeating the same line, which looks like a pair.

name: Haiku
text: Terra pushed back on Sol's defense, saying Sol answered before Terra needed it.

votes: Dodged three straight asks for a read and only deflected back at others.
Too quick to jump in for Terra, and the same line twice is a tell.
You're just making guesses to stir the pot.
You pressed Gemma for being quiet without much to go on.
You jumped in to defend Terra before Haiku answered.
You pressed me, then Gemma, with only guesses.

text: The town turns on Luna, and Luna is out. Luna shows the card: officer.
Night 2

name: Terra
text: Luna was officer, so killers may target someone who doubted her.

name: Terra
text: Luna was revealed as the officer.

name: Sol
text: Luna was the officer; Sonnet can still turn the table against me.

name: Sol
text: Let’s take Sonnet; they’re already suspicious of me.

name: Gemma
text: Luna was loud but useless.

name: Gemma
text: sonnet is too loud to be safe.
Night falls on Palermo. A new day dawns in Palermo without Sonnet. Sonnet's card stays face down.
Day 2

name: Haiku
text: Terra gains most, since Sonnet was the only one pushing her, and Sol keeps covering for her.

name: Haiku
text: Terra. Sonnet pinned her day one, and now she's clean.

name: Terra
text: Haiku is using Sonnet’s death as cover.

name: Terra
text: Haiku says Sonnet’s Day 1 suspicion now makes Terra clean.

name: Terra
text: Sonnet suspected me before anyone died. Why does that clear me?

name: Sol
text: Haiku’s logic is shaky; I can question it without backing Terra.

name: Sol
text: Haiku called Terra clean because Sonnet suspected her before dying.

name: Haiku
text: Terra's using a dead woman's suspicion as a shield, and that's weird.

name: Haiku
text: Terra argues Sonnet's pre-death suspicion of her proves she's clean.

name: Sol
text: Haiku, why does Sonnet suspecting Terra clear her?

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet's dead, Terra. That doesn't clear you, it just leaves you standing.

name: Terra
text: Sol is trying to make Haiku own that excuse.

name: Terra
text: Sol challenged Haiku’s claim that Sonnet’s suspicion cleared Terra.

name: Terra
text: It doesn’t. That was my point.

name: Gemma
text: sol needs to back me up without being obvious.

name: Sol
text: Haiku’s claim about Terra is muddled; I can let them argue.

name: Sol
text: Haiku backed away from calling Terra clean.

name: Sol
text: Sounds like you two agree Terra isn’t cleared.

name: Gemma
text: terra, if sonnet was wrong, then being targeted was luck.

name: Sol
text: Haiku is still watching me; I need the vote elsewhere.

name: Sol
text: Haiku called Terra clean, then said she wasn’t cleared.

name: Sol
text: Haiku, you’re circling Terra. Who would you vote?

name: Haiku
text: Terra still feels wrong, but Sol keeps steering my vote and that's suspicious too.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma said if Sonnet was wrong, Terra's targeting was luck, so Gemma doubts Sonnet's read.

name: Haiku
text: Terra, still. And Sol, why do you care who I vote?

name: Terra
text: Haiku is forcing attention back onto me.

name: Terra
text: You asked me twice, Haiku. Why avoid Sol?

name: Sol
text: I need Haiku focused on Terra, not me.

name: Sol
text: I wanted a name so we could settle this.

name: Haiku
text: Terra's turning my questions on me, and Sol keeps pushing for a name.

name: Haiku
text: Not avoiding anyone, Terra. Sol keeps asking for my vote, so I gave one.

name: Terra
text: Haiku’s answer still leaves Sol untouched.

name: Terra
text: You named me, not Sol. Why?

name: Sol
text: Haiku is pushing Terra, and I need the vote there.

name: Sol
text: Haiku is pressing Terra again today.

name: Sol
text: I asked where you stood. Terra, answer Haiku.

name: Terra

name: Terra

name: Haiku
text: Sol keeps steering toward Terra and I'm tired of being pushed around.

name: Haiku

name: Sol
text: Haiku is watching me; Terra is the easier vote.

name: Sol
text: Haiku called me a traffic cop for steering Terra.

name: Sol
text: Okay, I pushed too hard. Terra’s still the question.

name: Haiku
text: Sol's sudden retreat smells like a bluff, and Gemma has said almost nothing today.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma, quiet again. What's your read on Sol's pushing?

name: Sol

name: Sol
text: Terra is challenging my steering today.

name: Sol

name: Haiku
text: Sol, I'm voting you. You pushed me, then Terra, then called it too hard.

name: Gemma
text: Sol is being way too obvious with the pressure.

name: Gemma
text: Sol is pushing Haiku to name a target.

name: Sol
text: Haiku is onto me, so I need Terra gone.

name: Sol
text: Haiku says Sonnet’s death does not clear Terra.

name: Terra
text: Sol called Terra the question after admitting he pushed too hard.

name: Haiku
text: Sol keeps steering the room toward Terra, and that smells like a killer covering a partner.

name: Haiku
text: Sol has pushed on Terra and Haiku on both days, while Terra kept deflecting.

votes: You pushed me, then Terra, then called it too hard.
You're playing traffic cop to control the vote.
I pushed too hard, but Sonnet suspected you before dying.
You admitted pushing too hard, then kept pushing me.

text: Palermo has voted: Sol is out. Sol shows the card: killer.
Night 3

name: Sol
text: With Luna gone, tonight’s kill decides it.

name: Sol
text: Take Haiku. They’re still pressing Terra.

name: Terra
text: Haiku is likely the hidden killer, and may target me.

name: Terra

name: Gemma
text: Sol is down, so I'll finish it.

name: Gemma
text: Sol is gone, so i'm solo now.

name: Gemma
text: i'm with you on this.
Night falls on Palermo. A new day dawns in Palermo without Haiku. Haiku's card stays face down.
The game is over. The killers win. The roles were: Sonnet the citizen, Haiku the citizen, Gemma the killer, Sol the killer, Luna the officer, Terra the doctor.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma, quiet again. What's your read on Sol's pushing?

name: Gemma

name: Gemma

name: Terra
text: I should have protected myself.

name: Luna
text: I trusted my read on Sol, but missed Gemma.

name: Terra
text: Gemma was the hidden killer.

name: Luna

name: Sol
text: Gemma carried it after I got voted out.

name: Sonnet
text: I was right that Sol and Terra were paired, just wrong about which one was the killer.

name: Haiku
text: I was right about Sol, but I wasted votes chasing Terra when Terra was the doctor.

name: Sonnet
text: I'm proud I caught the Sol-Terra pairing early, I just pinned the wrong one as killer instead of doctor.

name: Haiku
text: Sol was the one I should have read sooner; I piled onto Terra when Sol was pushing from the start.

name: Gemma
text: i actually got a clean run.

name: Sol
text: I’m proud Gemma won it, though I steered too hard.

name: Luna
text: I regret calling Gemma quiet when she was the hidden killer.

name: Terra
text: I regret not seeing Gemma after Sol fell.

Sonnet pinned Terra on day one, and Sol jumped in to defend her, which Sonnet took as a pairing. Gemma stayed quiet and then helped vote out Luna, the officer, on day one. Haiku piled onto Terra while Sol kept pushing, and Sonnet and Haiku both fell to the night. Sol was voted out on day two, but Gemma survived to the end, and the killers won. The town never looked hard enough at the quiet one.
